source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #298 (branch fix/134-filesystem-contract at head 62e3b88d11f1f1d6eb3032a8500b4562c3bfaad2 — branch commit a83777e (make wasi:filesystem read-only by contract (#134)), merge commit d6e6aa8 bringing in current main 6d29650 (PR #297, #135), and fix commit 62e3b88 (is-same-object: compare filesystem identity, not canonical paths); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45359403134 and 45359413144 against the branch and pull-request run 45359097175, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #298 (#134, wasi:filesystem read-only contract). The PR adds an exclude option to the component bindgen so named functions are omitted from the generated add_to_linker, excludes the twelve mutating filesystem functions from registration (write, write-via-stream, append-via-stream, set-size, set-times, set-times-at, create-directory-at, remove-directory-at, rename-at, unlink-file-at, link-at, symlink-at), implements the remaining seven non-mutating functions (advise, sync, sync-data, readlink-at, is-same-object, metadata-hash, metadata-hash-at), rejects mutate-directory opens in open-at, and — after a Codex P2 finding — makes is-same-object compare filesystem identity from fs::metadata ((device, inode) on Unix, (volume serial, file index) on Windows, canonical-path fallback) instead of canonical path strings. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone (workflow_dispatch run 45359420790, gate success). Unlike the previous rounds, that control does not reproduce the checked-in baseline on the eight wasi and wasi-threads gated series: PR #297 (#135, wasi:sockets stub removal) landed on main after the PR #294 re-baseline and shrank those series itself, and the size gate only fails on growth, so no re-baseline was taken then. This update therefore absorbs both parts, split by the control measurement. PR #297's part (checked-in baseline to main control): in release, wasi and wasi-threads each shrink by 96,960 B stripped file / 71,424 B stripped .text; in release-size, wasi shrinks by 62,448 B / 41,952 B and wasi-threads by 62,448 B / 41,936 B. This PR's own part (main control to branch): 8 of the 32 gated series change, all in wasi and wasi-threads and all shrinking — in release, wasi shrinks by 19,456 B stripped file / 14,256 B stripped .text and wasi-threads by 19,440 B / 14,256 B; in release-size, wasi shrinks by 12,288 B / 8,096 B and wasi-threads by 12,272 B / 8,096 B. Every other gated series, including the baseline configuration, is unchanged. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is unchanged: the release component stripped file series at +9.60% (2,433,656 B to 2,667,344 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series across the three samples.
